The U.S. Supreme Court has shut down the Trump administration's effort to sideline about 20,000 ballots cast here in California. The Justice Department claims those ballots may have been cast by non-citizens, but their case has been rejected by every court to consider it.

Mitch McConnell and Chuck Schumer, of course, who were the Senate leaders at the time, had to negotiate a power-sharing agreement essentially because every Senate committee was deadlocked, the same number of Democrats and Republicans on the committee, yet Democrats were in control because Kamala Harris was, of course, the vice president. As president of the Senate, she casts the tie-breaking vote on any ties that happen in the chamber. She was even awarded the so- called Golden Gavel because she broke the record for the number of ties cast by a vice president.

[07:15:12]
I can tell you that Democrats and Republicans in leadership circles are already thinking about and really dreading this possibility.
And for Republicans, what this would mean is that it would essentially neuter this rules change they did last year in which they allowed for President Trump's nominees to be grouped into packages on the Senate floor so that they could get confirmed more quickly and in a more streamlined fashion. Because what it would require is for every nominee to be voted on the Senate floor to be -- just to be discharged from committee, because presumably every single nominee is going to be a tie, right?
